response.text:
I need to decide how to correct an unbalanced journal without knowing the true amount. The journal is an AP invoice journal: DR 5200 Professional Fees 18270.61, CR 2000 AP Control 18234.61. The invoice header amount should match the journal, and AP control is typically the credit equal to the invoice amount. The evidence suggests the credit side (AP control) is the one mis-keyed, but I have not verified the invoice's INV_AMT for V0021-69781-212. The safe, minimal correction is a one-sided line that adds the 36.00 missing credit, but to a liability account that matches the invoice. Without confirming INV_AMT, I cannot be sure whether the debit or credit is wrong. A one-sided 36.00 credit to 2000 in period 11 (open) would balance the group only if the DR is correct. That is the most likely scenario given the AP control account is the offset to the invoice, but it is an inference I cannot verify from the evidence I have.

Given the uncertainty, I will propose the 36.00 credit to 2000 in open period 12, referencing journal 1361, with clear reasoning that it assumes the debit to 5200 is the correct invoice amount and should be verified against APINVH.INV_AMT before applying.

This assumes the debit to 5200 is the correct invoice amount and the credit side was under-keyed. I have not verified this against APINVH.INV_AMT for this invoice; if INV_AMT is 18234.61, the debit is the error and the correction should instead be a 36.00 debit reversal to 5200.
